summary: This TurtleBot 4 User Manual tutorial explains how to navigate a robot using localization on an existing map, as opposed to SLAM, which builds the map while navigating. It covers launching the Nav2 navigation stack on a physical TurtleBot 4 and in the Ignition simulator for both Galactic and Humble ROS 2 distributions, and describes the Rviz2 navigation tools: 2D Pose Estimate, Publish Point and Nav2 Goal. The page also includes navigation and documentation boilerplate that was ignored.
one_line: Tutorial on localizing and navigating a TurtleBot 4 on an existing map using the Nav2 stack, launch commands, and Rviz2 tools.
key_facts: SLAM generates a map as the robot navigates and is useful for unknown or dynamic environments, but cannot see areas it has not yet discovered.
Localization uses an existing map along with live odometry and laserscan data to determine the robot's position on the map.
Localization does not update the map when the environment changes, but the robot can still avoid new obstacles, giving more repeatable navigation results.
The TurtleBot 4 uses the Nav2 stack for navigation.
On a physical TurtleBot 4 in Galactic, navigation is launched with nav_bringup.launch.py using slam:=off localization:=true map:=office.yaml.
In the Ignition simulator in Galactic, the default world is depot and uses the existing depot.yaml map file.
In Humble, the physical robot localization is launched with localization.launch.py map:=office.yaml and then nav2.launch.py is launched in another terminal.
In Humble, the simulator defaults to the warehouse world and uses the warehouse.yaml map file.
When using multiple robots through the namespacing method, a namespace parameter such as namespace:=/robot1 must be passed to both the Localization and Nav2 launch files.
An initial pose is required before navigation can begin.
Rviz is launched on the physical robot with ros2 launch turtlebot4_viz view_robot.launch.py.
The 2D Pose Estimate tool sets the approximate initial pose of the robot on the map, which Nav2 needs to start localizing.
The Publish Point tool publishes clicked map coordinates to the /clicked_point topic.
The Nav2 Goal tool sets a goal pose; Nav2 plans a path and drives the robot there, and the initial pose should be set first.
